title: SharePoint: chat one-on-one with SharePoint agents in Teams
summary: The roadmap facts, control paths, commands and licensing statements are supported. The page needs minor corrections to acknowledge differing Microsoft guidance on content discovery and multiple agents in Teams, and to reconcile checklist controls with its table.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Responses follow the asking user's data permissions and exclude content from sources the user cannot access.
claims.quote: if a user has access to the agent but not to the site or document library it references, the agent's responses for this user don't include content from those restricted sources.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: SharePoint sites, pages and document libraries are knowledge sources, and their permissions control users' access to information through agents.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint use SharePoint sites, pages, and document libraries as knowledge sources to respond to the user. You can control a user's access to the information when they use an agent by controlling their access to the site.

claims.claim: Microsoft is retiring the .agent file format, rather than retiring all agents in SharePoint.
claims.quote: No, only the .agent file format is being retired.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Existing .agent files continue working across SharePoint, Teams and the Copilot app until the end of March 2027.
claims.quote: Existing agents in the .agent file format will continue to work across SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, and the Copilot app until the end of March 2027.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: .agent files in Teams chats or channels stop responding after March 2027 and require upgrade for continued use.
claims.quote: After March 2027, .agent files will stop responding and you will have to upgrade to continue using them.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Permissions on a .agent file determine who can access the agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the `.agent` file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.claim: Permissions on a .agent file determine who can edit the agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the `.agent` file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.claim: All .agent agents in a single Teams chat must be upgraded at the same time.
claims.quote: you need to upgrade all agents used in the chat at the same time or else one upgraded agent will render all other (.agent file) agents unusable.
claims.fix: Keep the upgrade guidance, but add: 'Microsoft's Teams-sharing training instead says only one agent can be added at a time; the training and upgrade guidance differ on multiple agents in a chat.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/training/modules/use-no-code-agents-sharepoint/3-share-agent-microsoft-teams.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Blocking a SharePoint-created agent affects Microsoft Copilot Chat only, not Teams.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The block action applies to the selected agent across the organisation, subject to the stated SharePoint host limitation.
claims.quote: Block or unblock agents for the entire organization by using the same controls that work for any other app in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The block control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **All agents**. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The Graph block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: expand **Sites** and select **Active sites**. ... Select the site you want to configure. ... Open the **Settings** tab, and then turn **Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot** on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery for a site.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery hides the Agent icon in the site's global header.
claims.quote: Once you flag a site with restricted content discovery, users can't see the Agent icon on the global header of the site.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery prevents the site's content from being surfaced in Microsoft Copilot or organisation-wide search.
claims.quote: The restricted content discovery policy leaves site access unchanged but prevents the site's content from being surfaced in Microsoft Copilot or organization-wide search for all users.
claims.fix: Qualify the statement everywhere it appears: 'Restricted Content Discovery limits organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, but does not affect experiences operating on content already in use, such as summarising an open document.' The latter qualification is in the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery FAQ and narrows the access-management page's broader wording.

claims.claim: The Restricted Content Discovery page does not describe an effect specific to Teams chat.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams chat actions Restricted Content Discovery. Read restricted-content-discovery in full and manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint; discovery scope is documented, but the Restricted Content Discovery page does not describe Teams chat specifically.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Delegating Restricted Content Discovery management to site administrators is a separate tenant setting.
claims.quote: If you want site administrators to manage the setting for their own sites, enable delegation ... Set-SPOTenant -DelegateRestrictedContentDiscoverabilityManagement $true

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires organisational Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires SharePoint Advanced Management to be available.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents pay-as-you-go applies to .agent files.
claims.quote: SharePoint Agents pay-as-you-go only applies to .agent files. The upgraded agents follow the capabilities and licensing model for agents in Microsoft Copilot app.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects Copilot-licensed access and consumption-based access.
